correctness.summary: A one-edge maximal matching is a dominating edge. Its endpoint-neighborhood partition makes the cyclomatic number equal the number of common neighbors; for r>=2 the dominating edge is unique, every other maximal matching has size two, and exact counting gives the claimed bound and equality structure. Finite exact enumeration agrees.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: Zhang (2026) solves the bicyclic minimum and quotes the Engbers-Erey extension question for k-cyclic graphs. The present cyclomatic bound recovers the bicyclic theorem at r=2 and extends its minimum mechanism to every r>=2 in the range n>=r+2. Searches did not locate the all-r formula or equality classification.

value.summary: The theorem replaces bicyclic core casework by a general dominating-edge mechanism and gives an exact unique extremal graph for every r>=2 and n>=r+2, directly advancing the minimum side of the k-cyclic extension problem.

limitations: The exact fixed-(n,r) minimum is established only for n>=r+2; the denser range n<r+2 is not classified.
The maximum side of the k-cyclic extremal problem is not addressed.
The full text of Engbers and Erey (2023) was not inspected; its relevant scope and extension question were checked through Zhang (2026).
Originality is to the best of our knowledge; differently indexed or very recent work remains a residual risk.
Finite computation supports but does not replace the proof.
